translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the twelfth month Liu Yu shattered Lu Xun at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 七年春二月壬午，右將軍劉籓斬徐道覆于始興，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Seventh year, spring, second month, renwu day: Liu Fan, Right General, beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing; head transmitted to capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the second month of spring Liu Fan executed Xu Daofu at Shixing and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，盧循走交州，刺史杜慧度斬之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Lu Xun fled to Jiaozhou; Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's fourth month Lu Xun fled to Jiaozhou, where Du Huidu killed him.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁卯，以荊州刺史劉道規爲征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingmao day: Liu Daogui, Inspector of Jingzhou, was made General Who Conquers the West with ceremony equal to the Three Elders and independent office.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Liu Daogui of Jingzhou became General Who Conquers the West with Three Elders honors and an independent command.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，沮渠蒙遜伐涼，涼武昭王玄盛與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Juqu Mengxun attacked Liang; Martial Illustrious King Xuansheng of Liang fought him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Juqu Mengxun invaded Hexi, but Li Xuansheng—honored as Martial Illustrious King of Liang—met him in battle and won.

sentences.zh: 八年春二月丙子，以吳興太守孔靖爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Eighth year, spring, second month, bingzi day: Kong Jing, Administrator of Wuxing, was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the second month of spring in the eighth Yixi year Kong Jing of Wuxing became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，山陰地陷四尺，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Third month, jiayin day: in Shanyin the earth sank four chi; there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the third month the ground near Shanyin dropped four feet amid thunderous rumbling.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，乞伏公府弑乞伏乾歸，乾歸子熾盤誅公府，僭卽偽位。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: Qifu Gongfu murdered Qifu Gangui; Gangui's son Chipan executed Gongfu and usurped the false position.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's fifth month Qifu Gongfu assassinated Qifu Gangui; Gangui's son Qifu Chipan avenged him, slew Gongfu, and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 六月，以平北將軍魯宗之爲鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Lu Zongzhi, General Who Pacifies the North, was made General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Lu Zongzhi advanced from General Who Pacifies the North to General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲午，武陵王季度薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jiawu day: Prince Jidu of Wuling died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in autumn's seventh month Prince Sima Jidu of Wuling died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，征西大將軍劉道規卒。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day, Liu Daogui, General Who Conquers the West, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Liu Daogui, General Who Conquers the West, passed away.

sentences.zh: 八月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，高密王純之薨。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day, Prince Chunzhi of Gaomi died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Prince Sima Chunzhi of Gaomi died.

sentences.zh: 九月癸酉，葬僖皇后于休平陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month, guiyou day: Empress Xi was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day in the ninth month Empress Xi was interred at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己卯，太尉劉裕害右將軍兗州刺史劉籓、尚書左僕射謝混。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, Grand Commandant Liu Yu harmed Liu Fan, Right General and Inspector of Yanzhou, and Xie Hun, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Liu Yu as Grand Commandant eliminated Liu Fan—Right General and governor of Yanzhou—and Xie Hun, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，裕矯詔曰：「劉毅苞藏禍心，構逆南夏，籓、混助亂，志肆姦宄。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day, Yu forged an edict stating: "Liu Yi harbors a treacherous heart and plotted rebellion in southern Xia; Fan and Hun abetted chaos and indulged villainy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Liu Yu forged an edict accusing Liu Yi of concealed treason and rebellion across the south, with Liu Fan and Xie Hun abetting the plot.

sentences.zh: 賴寧輔玄鑒，撫機挫銳，凶黨卽戮，社稷乂安。

translations.literal: Thanks to the protector's subtle insight, grasping the moment and blunting their edge—the villainous party was forthwith executed; the altars of soil and grain are again secure.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to wise ministers who seized the moment and broke their strength, the traitors fell at once and the dynasty stood firm.

sentences.zh: 夫好生之德，所因者本，肆眚覃仁，實資玄澤。

translations.literal: Now the virtue of cherishing life takes root in fundamentals; extending forgiveness spreads benevolence—it truly depends on profound grace.
translations.idiomatic: The love of life grows from fundamental goodness; broad pardon spreads humane rule through deepest grace.

sentences.zh: 況事興大憝，禍自元凶。

translations.literal: Moreover when affairs produce great villains, calamity stems from the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion rises from its prime mover, guilt rests first on the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 其大赦天下，唯劉毅不在其例。

translations.literal: Accordingly there is general amnesty under heaven; only Liu Yi is not within the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be amnesty for all under heaven—except Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 普增文武位一等。

translations.literal: Universally raise civil and military rank one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Advance every civil and military officer one rank.

sentences.zh: 孝順忠義，隱滯遺逸，必令聞達。

translations.literal: Filial, obedient, loyal, righteous—those hidden, stranded, or overlooked—must be caused to become heard and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Filial sons and steadfast loyalists still in obscurity shall be brought forward until their names are known.

sentences.zh: 」己丑，劉裕帥師討毅。

translations.literal: " On the jichou day, Liu Yu led troops to punish Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " On jichou day Liu Yu marched against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 裕參軍王鎮惡陷江陵城，毅自殺。

translations.literal: Yu aide Wang Zhene seized Jiangling city; Yi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e, Liu Yu's adjutant, stormed Jiangling; Liu Yi committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，沮渠蒙遜僭號河西王。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Juqu Mengxun styled himself King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Juqu Mengxun proclaimed himself King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以西陵太守朱齡石爲建威將軍、益州刺史，帥師伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiling, was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yizhou and led troops to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhu Lingshi of Xiling became General Who Establishes Might and governor of Yizhou, then led the expedition into Shu.

sentences.zh: 分荊州十郡置湘州。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies were split from Jingzhou to establish Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court carved ten commanderies out of Jingzhou to create Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，廬陵、南康地四震。

translations.literal: This year Luling and Nankang earth shook four times.
translations.idiomatic: That year the earth trembled four times in Luling and Nankang.

sentences.zh: 九年春三月丙寅，劉裕害前將軍諸葛長民及其弟輔國大將軍黎民、從弟寧朔將軍秀之。

translations.literal: Ninth year, spring, third month, bingyin day: Liu Yu harmed Zhuge Changmin, Former General; his younger brother Liming, Grand General Who Supports the State; and cousin Xiu Zhi, General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the third month of spring Liu Yu eliminated Zhuge Changmin—Former General—together with his brother Zhuge Liming, Grand General Who Supports the State, and his cousin Zhuge Xiuzhi, General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，加劉裕鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day, Liu Yu was additionally given General Who Garrisons the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Liu Yu added the titles General Who Garrisons the West and governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 林邑范胡達寇九真，交州刺史杜慧度斬之。

translations.literal: Fan Huda of Linyi raided Jiuzhen; Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Huda of Linyi struck Jiuzhen until Du Huidu of Jiaozhou executed him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，罷臨沂、湖熟皇后脂澤田四十頃，以賜貧人，弛湖池之禁。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, renxu day: forty qing of empress cosmetic-fields at Linyi and Hushu were abolished to give to poor people; prohibitions on lakes and ponds were relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in summer's fourth month the court surrendered forty qing of imperial wardrobe estates at Linyi and Hushu to the needy and lifted restrictions on fishing and foraging in public waters.

sentences.zh: 封鎮北將軍魯宗之爲南陽郡公。

translations.literal: Lu Zongzhi, General Who Guards the North, was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, General Who Guards the North, received the ducal title for Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Zhu Lingshi took Chengdu, beheaded Qiao Zong; Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn's seventh month Zhu Lingshi seized Chengdu, executed Qiao Zong, and restored order in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，封劉裕次子義真爲桂陽公。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yizhen—Liu Yu's second son—was invested as Duke of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，安平王球之薨。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Prince Qiuzhi of Anping died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter's twelfth month Prince Sima Qiuzhi of Anping died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高句麗、倭國及西南夷銅頭大師並獻方物。

translations.literal: This year Koguryŏ, Wa, and the Bronze-Head Master of the southwestern Yi all presented local produce.
translations.idiomatic: That year embassies arrived from Koguryŏ, Japan, and the southwestern chief styled Bronze-Head Master, each bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年春三月戊寅，地震。

translations.literal: Tenth year, spring, third month, wuyin day: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the third month of spring in the tenth Yixi year the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，乞伏熾盤帥師伐禿髮傉檀，滅之。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Qifu Chipan led troops to campaign against Tufa Nutan and extinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's sixth month Qifu Chipan invaded Southern Liang and destroyed Tufa Nutan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，淮北大風，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: north of the Huai great wind destroyed huts and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn's seventh month gales north of the Huai tore through dwellings.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, dingsi new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On new moon dingsi in the ninth month a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 林邑遣使來獻方物。

translations.literal: Linyi sent envoys to present local produce.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi dispatched ambassadors with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，城東府。

translations.literal: This year the Eastern Headquarters was walled.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court fortified the Eastern Headquarters compound.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，荊州刺史司馬休之、雍州刺史魯宗之並舉兵貳於劉裕，裕帥師討之。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, spring, first month: Sima Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jingzhou, and Lu Zongzhi, Inspector of Yongzhou, together raised troops in defiance of Liu Yu; Yu led troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eleventh Yixi year Sima Xiuzhi of Jingzhou and Lu Zongzhi of Yongzhou rebelled against Liu Yu, who took the field against them.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day, general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the throne proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以吏部尚書謝裕爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day, Xie Yu, Minister of Personnel, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Xie Yu advanced from Minister of Personnel to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二月丁未，姚興死，子泓嗣偽位。

translations.literal: Second month, dingwei day: Yao Xing died; his son Hong succeeded to the false position.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the second month Yao Xing died and his heir Yao Hong inherited the throne of Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，淮陵王蘊薨。

translations.literal: Third month, xinsi day: Prince Yun of Huailing died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the third month Prince Sima Yun of Huailing died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，劉裕及休之戰于江津，休之敗，奔襄陽。

translations.literal: On the renwu day, Liu Yu joined Xiuzhi in battle at Jiang Ford; Xiuzhi was defeated and fled to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Liu Yu defeated Sima Xiuzhi at the Jiangjin ford; Xiuzhi escaped toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，青、冀二州刺史劉敬宣爲其參軍司馬道賜所害。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, yimao day: Liu Jingxuan, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was murdered by his army aide Sima Daoci.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day in summer's fourth month Sima Daoci, Liu Jingxuan's adjutant, assassinated him—Liu held joint command of Qingzhou and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，彗星二見。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiashen day: two comets were seen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month observers noted two comets.

sentences.zh: 甲午，休之、宗之出奔于姚泓。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day, Xiuzhi and Zongzhi fled out to Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi took refuge with Yao Hong of Qin.

sentences.zh: 論平蜀功，封劉裕子義隆彭城公，朱齡石豐城公。

translations.literal: Discussing merit in pacifying Shu, Liu Yu's son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng; Zhu Lingshi as Duke of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarding the conquest of Shu, the court enfeoffed Liu Yilong as Duke of Pengcheng and Zhu Lingshi as Duke of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 己酉，霍山崩，出銅鐘六枚。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day, Mount Huo collapsed; six bronze bells came forth.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day a landslide on Mount Huo exposed six ancient bronze bells.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙戌，京師大水，壞太廟。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, bingxu day: great water at the capital; the Grand Temple was damaged.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day in autumn's seventh month floodwaters swamped the capital and damaged the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 辛亥晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On xinhai last day of month: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month xinhai a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 八月丁未，尚書左僕射謝裕卒，以尚書右僕射劉穆之爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Eighth month, dingwei day: Xie Yu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, died; Liu Muzhi, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Xie Yu died; Liu Muzhi moved from Right to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月己亥，大赦。

translations.literal: Ninth month, jihai day: general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the ninth month the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月，姚泓使其將魯軌寇襄陽，雍州刺史趙倫之擊走之。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, spring, first month: Yao Hong sent his general Lu Gui to raid Xiangyang; Zhao Lunzhi, Inspector of Yongzhou, struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twelfth Yixi year Yao Hong dispatched Lu Gui against Xiangyang, but Zhao Lunzhi of Yongzhou repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 二月，加劉裕中外大都督。

translations.literal: Second month: Liu Yu was additionally given Grand Commander-in-Chief of inner and outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Liu Yu received supreme command over every army at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，赫連勃勃攻姚泓秦州，陷之。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Helian Bobo attacked Yao Hong's Qinzhou and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's sixth month Helian Bobo overran Qinzhou for Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 己酉，新除尚書令、都鄉亭侯劉柳卒。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day, newly appointed Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Duxiang Liu Liu died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Liu Liu—just named Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Duxiang—died.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，劉裕及琅邪王德文帥衆伐姚泓。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Liu Yu and Prince of Langye Dewen led hosts to campaign against Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn's eighth month Liu Yu and Sima Dewen, Prince of Langye, marched west against Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大赦。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day the throne issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，姚泓將姚光以洛陽降。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, bingyin day: Yao Guang, Yao Hong's general, surrendered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in winter's tenth month Yao Guang handed Luoyang over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遣兼司空、高密王恢之修謁五陵。

translations.literal: On the jichou day, concurrently Minister of Works and Prince of Gaomi Huizhi was dispatched to repair worship at the Five Mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Prince Sima Huizhi of Gaomi—acting Minister of Works—was sent to repair and sacrifice at the eastern Jin imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月甲戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, spring, first month, jiaxu new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On new year's day jiaxu in the thirteenth Yixi year a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二月，涼武昭王李玄盛薨，世子士業嗣位爲涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: Second month: Martial Illustrious King of Liang Li Xuansheng died; heir Shiye succeeded as Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Xuansheng died; his heir Li Shiye became governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 三月，龍驤將軍王鎮惡大破姚泓將姚紹于潼關。

translations.literal: Third month: Wang Zhen'e, General Who Quickens as a Dragon, greatly defeated Yao Hong's general Yao Shao at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Shao's army at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 夏，劉裕敗魏將鵝青于河曲，斬青裨將阿薄干。

translations.literal: Summer: Liu Yu defeated Wei general E Qing at River Bend and beheaded Qing's lieutenant A Bogan.
translations.idiomatic: During the summer campaign Liu Yu defeated the Wei commander E Qing near the river bend and slew his deputy A Bogan.

sentences.zh: 是月，涼公李士業大敗沮渠蒙遜于鮮支澗。

translations.literal: That month Duke Li Shiye of Liang greatly defeated Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Li Shiye routed Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉裕克潼關。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Liu Yu took Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liu Yu forced Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，會稽王脩之薨。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day, Prince Xiuzhi of Kuaiji died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Prince Sima Xiuzhi of Kuaiji died.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，林邑獻馴象、白鸚鵡。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guihai day: Linyi presented tame elephants and white parrots.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the sixth month Linyi sent trained elephants and white parrots as tribute.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，劉裕克長安，執姚泓，收其彝器，歸諸京師。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Liu Yu took Chang'an, seized Yao Hong, gathered his ritual vessels, and returned them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn's seventh month Liu Yu captured Chang'an and Yao Hong, seized the Qin ritual bronzes, and shipped them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 南海賊徐道期陷廣州，始興相劉謙之討平之。

translations.literal: Bandit of Nanhai Xu Daoqi seized Guangzhou; Liu Qianzhi, Administrator of Shixing, attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoqi of Nanhai overran Guangzhou until Liu Qianzhi, prefect of Shixing, crushed the rising.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月辛未，左僕射、前將軍劉穆之卒。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, xinwei day: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Former General Liu Muzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in winter's eleventh month Liu Muzhi—Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Former General—died.

sentences.zh: 十四年春正月辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, spring, first month, xinsi day: general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the first month of spring in the fourteenth Yixi year the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈田子害龍驤將軍王鎮惡于長安。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi, Inspector of Qingzhou, harmed Wang Zhen'e, General Who Quickens as a Dragon, at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi of Qingzhou assassinated Wang Zhen'e at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，劉裕爲相國，進封宋公。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Liu Yu became Chancellor of State and advanced enfeoffment as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's sixth month Liu Yu received the chancellorship and was promoted to Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，以涼公士業爲鎮西將軍，封酒泉公。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Duke Shiye of Liang was made General Who Garrisons the West and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Li Shiye became General Who Garrisons the West and received the secondary title Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，赫連勃勃大敗王師于青泥北。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Helian Bobo greatly defeated the royal army north of Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Helian Bobo shattered Jin forces north of Qingni.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱齡石焚長安宮殿，奔于潼關。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi, Inspector of Yongzhou, burned Chang'an palaces and fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi of Yongzhou torched the Chang'an palaces and withdrew toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 尋又大潰，齡石死之。

translations.literal: Soon again great rout; Lingshi died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his army collapsed utterly and Zhu Lingshi perished.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，帝崩于東堂，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, wuyin day: the emperor died in the Eastern Hall; at the time age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the twelfth month the emperor died in the Eastern Hall at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 葬休平陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was interred at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝不惠，自少及長，口不能言，雖寒暑之變，無以辯也。

translations.literal: The emperor was not clever; from youth to adulthood he could not speak with his mouth; although cold and heat changed, there was no means to discriminate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been feeble-minded from childhood: he never learned to speak and could not tell cold from heat.

sentences.zh: 凡所動止，皆非己出。

translations.literal: For all movements and halts, none issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Every action he took was dictated by others.

sentences.zh: 故桓玄之纂，因此獲全。

translations.literal: Therefore when Huan Xuan usurped, because of this he obtained preservation.
translations.idiomatic: That helplessness was why Huan Xuan kept him alive through the usurpation.

sentences.zh: 初讖云「昌明之後有二帝」，劉裕將爲禪代，故密使王韶之縊帝而立恭帝，以應二帝云。

translations.literal: Initially a prophecy said "After Changming there will be two emperors"; Liu Yu was about to carry out abdication transfer, therefore secretly ordered Wang Shaozhi to strangle the emperor and establish Emperor Gong, to answer to two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had promised two emperors after Emperor Xiaowu—whose temple name was Changming—so Liu Yu, preparing to seize the throne, secretly had Wang Shaozhi strangle Emperor An and elevate Emperor Gong to satisfy the omen.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，加羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, left and right chief clerks, majors, and attendant gentlemen four persons were established; feather-canopy and drum band were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 5 the court assigned four senior staff—chief clerks, army majors, and attendant gentlemen—with imperial feather banners and musicians.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔曰：「大司馬明德懋親，大尉道勳光大，並徽序彝倫，燮和二氣，髦俊引領，思佐鼎飪。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, an edict stated: "The Grand Marshal brightens virtue and encourages kinship; the Grand Commandant's Way and merit shine broadly—together they splendidly order constant norms and harmonize the two qi; outstanding men crane their necks, wishing to assist the cauldron stew.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 12 an edict declared: "The Grand Marshal honors virtue and kin; the Grand Commandant's achievements illuminate the realm—both uphold moral order and harmonize heaven and earth. Talented men everywhere long to help season the imperial stew.

sentences.zh: 而雅尚沖挹，四門弗辟，誠合大雅謙虛之道，實違急賢贊世之務。

translations.literal: Yet they esteem emptiness and modesty; the four gates are not opened—it truly fits the Great Ya modest way, but truly violates the urgent task of aiding worthies and assisting the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cling to self-effacement and keep their gates closed—noble modesty, perhaps, but it frustrates the urgent need to enlist talent for the state.

sentences.zh: 昔蒲輪載徵，異人並出，東平開府，奇士向臻，濟濟之盛，朕有欽焉。

translations.literal: Formerly rush-wheeled carts summoned worthies; unusual men emerged together; Dongping opened office; extraordinary gentlemen arrived in throngs—the flourishing multitude—We admire it.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers summoned hermits with spring-powered carts and filled their halls—think of Dongping's recruitment—until worthy men crowded the court. That grandeur fills Us with reverence.

sentences.zh: 可敕二府，依舊辟召，必將明敭俊乂，嗣軌前賢矣。

translations.literal: May the two offices be ordered to recruit according to precedent—they will surely brightly raise outstanding men and continue the tracks of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Let both palaces resume normal recruitment; brilliant men will rise and follow the example of past sages.

sentences.zh: 」於是始辟召掾屬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they began recruiting aides and staff.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they reopened appointments for aides and clerks.

sentences.zh: 時太尉裕都督中外諸軍，詔曰：「大司馬地隆任重，親賢莫貳。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Yu commanded all military affairs within and without; an edict stated: "The Grand Marshal's position is lofty and responsibility heavy; kin and worthy—none second.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Yu as Grand Commandant commanded every army, an edict added: "The Grand Marshal's station is exalted and his burden grave—he stands above all princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 雖府受節度，可身無致敬。」

translations.literal: Although the office receives regulation, in person there need be no paying respect."
translations.idiomatic: Even though his bureau answers to him, no one need bow when meeting him in person."

sentences.zh: 劉裕之北征也，帝上疏，請帥所莅，啓行戎路，修敬山陵。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu northward campaigned, the emperor submitted a memorial requesting to lead what he presided over, set out on the military road, and cultivate reverence at the mountain mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched north, Emperor Gong memorialized to accompany the expedition, travel the campaign roads, and pay homage at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，乃與裕俱發。

translations.literal: The court followed this; thereupon he set out together with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and he departed with Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 及有司以卽戎不得奉辭陵廟，帝復上疏曰：「臣推轂閫外，將革寒暑，不獲展情埏璲私心罔極。

translations.literal: When the authorities held that because of taking up arms he could not offer farewell at mausoleum temples, the emperor again submitted a memorial stating: "Your subject pushes the wheel beyond the gate; about to endure cold and heat; unable to extend feeling at the sacred mounds—private heart without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Officials objected that active duty barred a palace visit to the tombs, so he memorialized again: "I march beyond the capital and face years in the field; unable to bow at the ancestral shrines, my grief knows no bound.

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈，特垂聽許，使臣微誠粗申，卽路無恨。

translations.literal: We humbly hope for heavenly compassion, especially to drop ear and permit, causing your subject's slight sincerity roughly to extend—upon the road without regret.
translations.idiomatic: May Heaven grant a father's mercy and allow this humble plea, so my devotion finds some outlet and I march without regret.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: " It was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne consented.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓滅，歸于京都。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was extinguished, he returned to the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong fell he returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月戊寅，安帝崩。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, twelfth month, wuyin day: Emperor An died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the twelfth month of Yixi 14 Emperor An died.

sentences.zh: 劉裕矯稱遺詔曰：「唯我有晉，誕膺明命，業隆九有，光宅四海。

translations.literal: Liu Yu falsely styled a testamentary edict stating: "Only We possess Jin; We greatly received the bright mandate; enterprise rises over the nine domains; light lodges within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu forged a deathbed edict: "Jin alone received Heaven's bright mandate; its enterprise spans the nine provinces and its glory fills the seas.

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，屬當多難，幸賴宰輔，拯厥顛覆。

translations.literal: We, with lacking virtue, have encountered many difficulties; fortunately relying on ministers and assistants, rescued its overturning.
translations.idiomatic: We lack virtue yet inherited the throne in troubled times; only the chief ministers saved the dynasty from ruin.

sentences.zh: 仍恃保祐，克黜禍亂，遂冕旒辰極，混一六合。

translations.literal: Still relying on protection and blessing, able to dismiss calamity and chaos; thereupon crown-tassels at the polar seat, merging and uniting the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven continued its favor: rebellion was crushed and We ascended the throne, reuniting the realm.

sentences.zh: 方憑阿衡，惟新洪業，而遘疾大漸，將遂弗興。

translations.literal: Just relying on the Yi Yin, renewing the great enterprise; but encountering illness greatly declining; about to follow not rising.
translations.idiomatic: We hoped to lean on our Yi Yin and renew the great enterprise, but grave illness pulls Us down—we shall not recover.

sentences.zh: 仰惟祖宗靈命。

translations.literal: We look up and consider the ancestral spirits' commands.
translations.idiomatic: We look to our ancestors' decree.

sentences.zh: 親賢是荷。

translations.literal: Kin and worthy are what is borne.
translations.idiomatic: The burden falls on a worthy kinsman.

sentences.zh: 咨爾大司馬、琅邪王，體自先皇，明德光懋，屬惟儲貳，衆望攸集。

translations.literal: You, Grand Marshal and Prince of Langye—body from former emperor; bright virtue splendidly flourishing; category is heir-apparent; multitude's expectation gathers there.
translations.idiomatic: To you, Sima Dewen—Grand Marshal and Prince of Langye—son of the late emperor, brilliant in virtue, marked as heir: all hearts already turn to you.

sentences.zh: 其君臨晉邦，奉係宗祀，允執其中，燮和天下。

translations.literal: May he lord over Jin state, attend and tie ancestral sacrifices, sincerely hold the middle, harmonize all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mount the throne of Jin, tend the ancestral shrines, hold fast the golden mean, and bring harmony to the realm.

sentences.zh: 闡揚末誥，無廢我高祖之景命。

translations.literal: Expand and raise final commands; do not abandon Our high ancestor's glorious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this final charge and do not dishonor the glorious mandate of our founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 」是日，卽帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: " That day, he assumed the imperial throne; general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年春正月壬辰朔，改元。

translations.literal: First year of Yuanxi, spring, first month, renchen new moon: era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: On new year's day renchen in the first month of Yuanxi 1 the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 以山陵未厝，不朝會。

translations.literal: Because mountain mausoleum was not yet laid to rest, no court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor An's tomb was unfinished there were no New Year audiences.

sentences.zh: 立皇后褚氏。

translations.literal: Lady Chu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 甲午，徵劉裕還朝。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day, Liu Yu was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Liu Yu was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，有星孛于太微西籓。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day, there was a broom star in the western fence of Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day a comet appeared in the western enclosure of the Taiwei asterism.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬安皇帝于休平陵。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day, Emperor An was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Emperor An was interred at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝受朝，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: The emperor received court; bells hung but no music.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong held court with bells suspended but no music—a sign of mourning.

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍劉道憐爲司空。

translations.literal: Liu Daolian, General Who Inspires Awe, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daolian, General Who Inspires Awe, became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，劉裕移鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Liu Yu shifted garrison to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Liu Yu transferred his headquarters to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 以劉懷慎爲前將軍、北徐州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Liu Huaishen was made Former General and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou; he garrisoned Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaishen became Former General and governor of northern Xuzhou, with headquarters at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉裕自解揚州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu personally relinquished Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yu resigned the Yangzhou governorship.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙酉，裕以其子桂陽公義真爲揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, yiyou day: Yu made his son Yizhen, Duke of Guiyang, Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in winter's tenth month Liu Yu installed his son Liu Yizhen—Duke of Guiyang—as governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, dinghai new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On new moon dinghai in the eleventh month a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛卯，裕加殊禮。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, xinmao day: Yu was added exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day in the twelfth month Liu Yu received extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 己卯，太史奏，黑龍四見于東方。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, Grand Clerks reported: black dragons four times appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the astronomers reported four sightings of black dragons in the eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 二年夏六月壬戌，劉裕至于京師。

translations.literal: Second year, summer, sixth month, renxu day: Liu Yu arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in summer's sixth month of Yuanxi 2 Liu Yu reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 傅亮承裕密旨，諷帝禪位，草詔，請帝書之。

translations.literal: Fu Liang received Yu's secret intention; indirectly advised the emperor to abdicate; drafted edict; requested the emperor write it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, acting on Liu Yu's orders, urged abdication, drafted the edict, and asked the emperor to copy it in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 帝欣然謂左右曰：「晉氏久已失之，今復何恨。

translations.literal: The emperor gladly said to attendants: "The Jin house long ago lost it; now again what regret?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants willingly: "House Jin forfeited the mandate long ago—why resent yielding it now?

sentences.zh: 」乃書赤紙爲詔。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote red paper as edict.
translations.idiomatic: " He copied the abdication onto red paper.

sentences.zh: 甲子，遂遜于琅邪第。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day, thereupon he yielded at Langye residence.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day he abdicated and withdrew to the Langye princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 劉裕以帝爲零陵王，居于秣陵，行晉正朔，車旗服色一如其舊，有其文而不備其禮。

translations.literal: Liu Yu made the emperor Prince of Lingling; he dwelt at Moling; practiced Jin correct calendar; carriage banners clothing colors all as before old—having their pattern but not completing their ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu named him Prince of Lingling and housed him at Moling; Jin calendar and regalia remained in form, but ceremony was hollow.

sentences.zh: 帝自是之後，深慮禍機，褚後常在帝側，飲食所資，皆出褚后，故宋人莫得伺其隟，宋永初二年九月丁丑，裕使後兄叔度請后；

translations.literal: After this the emperor deeply feared crisis mechanisms; Empress Chu constantly remained at the emperor's side; whatever supplied drink and food all came from Empress Chu; therefore Song men could not spy his crack; Song Yongchu second year, ninth month, dingchou day, Yu ordered Empress Chu's elder brother Shudu to summon the empress;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Gong lived in dread of assassination; Empress Chu never left his side, and every meal passed through her hands so Liu Yu's agents found no opening. In Yongchu 2 of Song, on dingchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu had Empress Chu's brother Chu Shudu summon her away;

sentences.zh: 有間，兵人逾垣而入，弑帝于內房。

translations.literal: After an interval, soldiers climbed over the wall and entered; they murdered the emperor in the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later soldiers scaled the wall and stabbed him to death in his private rooms.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: At the time age thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 諡恭皇帝，葬沖平陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Emperor Gong; buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Emperor Gong and was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝幼時性頗忍急，及在籓國，曾令善射者射馬爲戲。

translations.literal: In childhood the emperor's nature was rather cruel and impatient; when in his princedom he once ordered skilled archers to shoot horses as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was harsh and hasty; while ruling his princedom he once staged archery contests that targeted horses.

sentences.zh: 旣而有人云：「馬者國姓，而自殺之，不祥之甚。

translations.literal: Afterwards someone said: "Horse is the dynastic surname; yet killing them oneself—inauspicious in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: "Horse echoes Sima—the imperial surname—and shooting those beasts yourself is a dreadful omen.

sentences.zh: 」帝亦悟，甚悔之。

translations.literal: " The emperor also understood and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He took the point and bitterly regretted the sport.

sentences.zh: 其後復深信浮屠道，鑄貨千萬，造丈六金像，親于瓦官寺迎之，步從十許里。

translations.literal: Afterward he again deeply believed in the Buddha Way; he cast cash in the tens of millions; built a sixteen-foot golden image; personally welcomed it at Waguan Temple; walked following ten-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he embraced Buddhism fervently, poured millions of cash into a sixteen-foot gilded statue, and welcomed it in person at Waguan Temple, walking in procession for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 安帝旣不惠，帝每侍左右，消息溫涼寢食之節，以恭謹聞，時人稱焉。

translations.literal: Emperor An already lacked cleverness; the emperor always attended left and right, regulating warmth and coolness and sleeping and eating rhythms; by respectful caution was heard of; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor An was helpless, Emperor Gong stayed constantly at his side, tending every comfort of clothing, food, and sleep—his devotion won praise across the court.

sentences.zh: 始，元帝以丁丑歲稱晉王，置宗廟，使郭璞筮之，云「享二百年。

translations.literal: Initially Yuan-di in the dingchou year styled Prince of Jin, established ancestral temples, ordered Guo Pu to divine them; it said "Enjoy two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan of Jin took the princely title in the dingchou year he founded the temples and had Guo Pu cast the oracle: "The house shall endure two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 」自丁丑至禪代之歲，年在庚申，爲一百四歲。

translations.literal: " From dingchou to the year of abdication transfer, year star at gengshen—it makes one hundred four years.
translations.idiomatic: " From dingchou to the abdication in gengshen is only one hundred four years.

sentences.zh: 然丁丑始係西晉，庚申終入宋年，所餘惟一百有二歲耳。

translations.literal: Yet dingchou begins tied to Western Jin; gengshen ends entering Song year—what remains is only one hundred two years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dingchou still belonged to Western Jin, while gengshen fell under Liu Song—the Eastern Jin segment spans only one hundred two years.

sentences.zh: 璞蓋以百二之期促，故婉而倒之爲二百也。

translations.literal: Pu probably took the hundred-two period as short; therefore tactfully inverted it to become two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu seems to have rounded up—finding one hundred two years too cramped he politely inverted the digits to "two hundred."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：安帝卽位之辰，鐘無妄之日，道子、元顯並傾朝政，主昏臣亂，未有如斯不亡者也。

translations.literal: The historians say: On the hour Emperor An assumed the throne—the Zhong Wuwang day—Daozi and Yuanxian together overturned court governance; ruler dim, ministers chaotic—never had there been such without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor An took the throne under baleful omens while Sima Daozi and Sima Yuanxian hijacked the government—a witless sovereign and treacherous ministers; never had a dynasty looked less likely to survive.

sentences.zh: 雖有手握戎麾，心存舊國，迴首無良，忽焉蕭散。

translations.literal: Although some grasped military banners and harbored the old state in heart—turning head without good—suddenly scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Even commanders who still clutched their batons and cherished Jin looked round for allies and found none; their efforts dissolved overnight.

sentences.zh: 於是桓玄乘釁，勢逾飆指，六師咸泯，隻馬徂遷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huan Xuan exploited cracks; momentum exceeded whirlwind pointing; six armies all vanished; lone horses moved away.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan seized the moment and swept forward faster than a gale; imperial armies melted away until lone riders fled the field.

sentences.zh: 是以宋高非典午之臣，孫恩豈金行之寇。

translations.literal: Therefore Song Gaozu was not a minister of Dianwu; could Sun En be a bandit of the Metal Line?
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder Liu Yu—future Emperor Wu of Song—was never truly a servant of House Sima, or that Sun En was scarcely a mere rebel against the Jin element.

sentences.zh: 若乃世遇顛覆，則恭皇斯甚。

translations.literal: As for generations encountering overturn—then Emperor Gong was extreme in this.
translations.idiomatic: Among rulers caught in dynastic collapse, none suffered more than Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 於越之民，詎熏丹穴，會稽之侶，寧歎入臣。

translations.literal: People of Yuyue—how could they be smoked in cinnabar caves? Companions of Kuaiji—how could they sigh entering servitude?
translations.idiomatic: The folk of Wu and Yue were never destined for barbarian exile; the gentry of Kuaiji hardly regretted submitting when Heaven had shifted the mandate.

sentences.zh: 去皇屋而歸來，灑丹書而不恨。

translations.literal: Leaving the imperial house and returning; sprinkling red writing yet without regret.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down from the purple halls yet kept his honor; though branded by abdication edicts he bore no bitterness.

sentences.zh: 夫五運攸革，三微數盡，猶高秋彫候，理之自然。

translations.literal: Now the five circuits shift; three beginnings' reckoning exhausts—still like high autumn's withering season—principle's naturalness.
translations.idiomatic: When each cosmic phase ends and the calendar runs out, it is like late autumn stripping the trees—the way of nature.

sentences.zh: 觀其搖落，人有爲之流漣者也。

translations.literal: Observing its shaking fall—there are people who for it shed flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: Watching those leaves fall still draws tears from men of feeling.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：安承流湎，大盜斯張。

translations.literal: Encomium says: An inherited drift and drowned; great robbers then spread.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict reads: Emperor An drifted in dissipation while mighty usurpers rose unchecked.

sentences.zh: 恭乃寓命，他人是綱。

translations.literal: Gong then lodged mandate; others were the guideline.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong held only a borrowed throne; every rein lay in another's hands.

sentences.zh: 猶存周赧，始立懷王。

translations.literal: Still preserving Zhou Nan; beginning establishing Huai Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Like late Zhou keeping King Nan as figurehead while enthroning King Huai of Chu.

sentences.zh: 虛尊假號，異術同亡。

translations.literal: Empty honor false title—different methods same perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Empty titles and borrowed sovereignty—different paths to the same doom.
